name: Belsnickel
description: The ragged, fur-clad gift-giver who brings sweets in one hand and a switch in the other
origin: The Palatinate in south-west Germany, carried to Pennsylvania by German settlers

debut.title: Palatinate and Pennsylvania Dutch tradition
debut.era: brought to America in the 1700s and 1800s

legend: Some time before Christmas, there's a bang at the door and in comes the Belsnickel: dressed in tattered furs, his face masked or smeared with soot, a bag over his shoulder and a switch in his fist. He wants to know how the children have behaved. He might make them recite a verse or a prayer, then scatter sweets and nuts on the floor. Any child who grabs too greedily gets a rap on the knuckles. His name is usually read as Pelz-Nickel: Nicholas in furs.

myths.claim: The Belsnickel is an American invention.
myths.explanation: He came from the Palatinate and the Rhineland, and German immigrants brought him to Pennsylvania.

myths.claim: The Belsnickel both rewards and punishes.
myths.explanation: He carries treats and a switch, and children never quite know which they'll get.

myths.claim: He only comes on Christmas Eve.
myths.explanation: He usually turns up in the week or two before Christmas, a warning to behave before the big night.

powers: A switch in one hand, sweets in the other
An unsettling knock at the door
weaknesses: Children who don't snatch the sweets
legacy: Belsnickling, a Christmas mumming tradition in Nova Scotia
Dwight Schrute dresses as Belsnickel in The Office (US) episode Dwight Christmas (2012)
facts: The Belsnickel comes from the Palatinate region of south-west Germany
German settlers brought him to Pennsylvania, where he's part of Pennsylvania Dutch tradition
He wears ragged furs and sometimes a mask or a soot-blackened face
He carries a switch for the naughty and sweets or nuts for the good
He often visits a week or two before Christmas, not on Christmas Eve
Children might have to recite a verse or answer questions before he hands out treats
His name is usually read as Pelz-Nickel, Nicholas in furs
hostIntro: Hide the good biscuits. Tonight's guest asks the questions, and the wrong answer stings.
